scenes.say: Ever wonder why your SQL query is slow? Let’s see how join strategies make all the difference.

scenes.label: Plan
scenes.sub: Query plans reveal how SQL engines execute joins.
scenes.say: A query plan shows the steps your database takes to run a query, including which join algorithm it picks.
Hash joins work best for big, unsorted data. Merge joins need sorted inputs. Nested loop joins shine with small tables or good indexes.

scenes.title: Check the Join Algorithm
scenes.say: Run the explain command to see which join algorithm your query uses. It helps you spot performance issues fast.

scenes.question: Is a hash join always fastest?
scenes.wrong: Yes, hash join is always best.
scenes.right: No, merge join can be faster if data is sorted, and nested loop is best for small tables.
scenes.say: Don’t assume hash join is always fastest. The best algorithm depends on your data and indexes.
